report.summary: CI/test-infrastructure change: split Vitest into cached Worker/UI/component Turbo tasks with transit hashing, docs-only CI fast path that fails closed, concurrent Worker RPC/op groups using test-context expect and per-test cleanup, cached browser fixture builds and narrower phone Playwright coverage, with spec/CI docs updated. No blocking defects found. One non-blocking risk: a concurrent ops group mutates the module-global STEP_LIMITS table. Tests could not be executed in this sandbox (bun test needed approval); verification is by code reading.

findings.text: The "step runner rules" group is now describe.concurrent, but one case temporarily mutates the module-global STEP_LIMITS table that the DO runner in the same isolate reads. Sibling cases running at the same time (maxConcurrency 4) all run create ops through settings.read, so they get a 300 ms timeout. That breaks the AGENTS.md/CI.md rule to keep cases with global mocks sequential. The likely effect is extra retries on a loaded runner, not wrong assertions, since siblings do not assert on settings.read. Making this group sequential (or moving this case to a sequential group) fixes it. A CI run under load showing settings.read retries or TEMPOD_TIMEOUT in sibling create ops would confirm it.

evidence.why: Runs inside describe.concurrent("step runner rules"), so concurrent siblings that call seedWs/readyWs run settings.read with the shortened 300 ms timeout until the finally block restores it.

checked.risk: Tests: concurrency safety (test-context expect, shared spies/globals, cleanup) in the newly concurrent Worker groups
Failure paths / fail-closed: docs-only change classification (missing, invalid or unreachable base, fetch timeout, empty diff, renames)
Build/runtime environment: docs-only lint/format via bunx without node_modules, pinned tool versions, configs
Cache correctness: Turbo task inputs, transit hashing, Worker exclusion of UI/routes, fixture build outputs
Tests: Playwright project grep/tags, phone device taps, UI controls used by new steps
Spec/docs consistency and repository rules (CI budget, required check job, docs updated in same change)
Security: workflow input handling (base SHA via env, no secrets) — no platform/SDK contracts touched
